newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EA-Generali says to make new Creditanstalt bid.
newsitem.headline: EA-Generali says to make new Creditanstalt bid.

text.p: Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali said on Friday it would together with its partners submit a new offer for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt in time to meet a midnight government deadline.

It said it would update an offer made last October, when the group offered to pay nine billion schillings for the bulk of the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt and said it would sell the remaining shares in a secondary offering.
Savings bank Die Erste earlier said it had left the consortium, which also includes Germany's Commerzbank and Banca Commerciale Italiana, after the partners failed to disagree on a joint offer.
Die Erste had proposed to form a holding with the flagship bank which it would control even though it is just a third of the size of Creditanstalt.
"The consortium regrets that Die Erste did not see itself able at this point in time to be part of the updated offer," EA-Generali said in a statement.

The insurer, majority-owned by Italy's Assicurazioni Generali SpA, said it would submit its bid to investment house JP Morgan, the Austrian government's advisor in the privatisation process. Details of the offer were not made available. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
